chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from a man, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
A woman does not undo her hair when she performs ghusl from janabah.

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَتْ: she performed ghusl; she undertook the ritual bath
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: janabah; the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the female subject addressed in the ruling
key_terms.شَعْرَهَا: her hair; the hair that is not required to be undone

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to undo her hair for ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ghusl from janabah: a woman is not required to undo her hair when performing the ritual bath. It indicates facilitation in the laws of taharah and clarifies a practical detail of ritual purity.
